reviewedEvidence.title: Taiwan FTC blocks Grab’s proposed foodpanda acquisition
reviewedEvidence.summary: Taiwan’s FTC prohibited the combination on 21 October. It cited competition concerns including Uber’s approximately 13.1% economic stake in Grab and found the offered commitments insufficient.
reviewedEvidence.implication: Treat cross-ownership, information rights and remedies as early diligence issues in platform M&A. Taiwan’s decision is not an Indonesian merger ruling or a measured GoFood market-share gain.
reviewedEvidence.nextAction: Check issuer responses, appeal and transaction termination status, any applicable break-fee terms, and Indonesia-specific competition analysis before changing a deal case.
reviewedEvidence.limitations: No acquisition closing or purchase-price payment is established. An appeal or termination must be separately verified; a minority holding is not automatically legal control.

reviewedEvidence.title: Grab details merchant AI, driver waiting-location guidance and voice-enabled kitchen tools
reviewedEvidence.summary: Grab describes its Merchant AI Assistant, RideGuide Smart Destination and Cloud Printer. The assistant’s architecture has a Singapore patent; applications in Indonesia and other markets remain pending. Smart Destination is also in the patent-application process.
reviewedEvidence.implication: Useful GoFood and Gojek product benchmarks: actionable merchant advice, practical driver waiting spots and lower-friction order handling. A patent or application does not prove adoption or profit gains.
reviewedEvidence.nextAction: Compare merchant task completion, driver idle distance and kitchen-order errors in controlled pilots; confirm local rollout and intellectual-property scope.

reviewedEvidence.title: Grab launches ChatGPT training for Thai drivers and merchants
reviewedEvidence.summary: Grab targets over 3,000 Thai partners for training, within a regional goal above 30,000. Management reports 275,000 Thai merchants using its AI assistant and 120,000 drivers adopting its driver assistant. These are issuer-reported adoption figures, not measured profit gains.
reviewedEvidence.implication: Benchmark Gojek partner productivity, merchant support and AI partnerships; the Thailand rollout does not establish Indonesia adoption or lost GoTo share.
reviewedEvidence.nextAction: Compare partner engagement, task completion and incremental support costs; test build-versus-partner options before assigning earnings uplift.

reviewedEvidence.title: Grab schedules Q3 2026 results for 2 November
reviewedEvidence.summary: Grab’s IR overview lists a 14 October announcement scheduling Q3 results for 2 November 2026. No Q3 earnings figures are available from that announcement.
reviewedEvidence.implication: Align the next GoTo–Grab comparison around disclosed operating and credit metrics rather than mismatched reporting periods.
reviewedEvidence.nextAction: Update the head-to-head board after publication; keep current Q2 actuals and acquisition proposals separately labelled.

reviewedEvidence.title: Grab Thailand and OpenAI expand partner AI training through GrabAcademy
reviewedEvidence.summary: Grab announced ChatGPT training for more than 3,000 Thai drivers, riders and restaurant operators. The release reports over 275,000 merchants using its merchant AI assistant and over 120,000 drivers using its driver assistant.
reviewedEvidence.implication: Pair merchant and driver AI tools with practical training, then measure workflow adoption and incremental partner earnings rather than attendance alone.
reviewedEvidence.nextAction: Test a limited GoFood Merchant / driver cohort against a matched holdout; assess task success, repeat use, support demand, cost and partner outcomes.
reviewedEvidence.limitations: Thailand figures are company-reported and not Indonesia counts. This 14 October source is newly reviewed backfill; training reach and tool use do not prove improved earnings.
